text: Welcome to week six of the official
Arkham Menard's iRacing series. And this
week, you'll be doing battle at the
Langley Speedway for 55 laps. For
qualifying, your time to heat up your
tires for the final lap will be limited.
But don't do it this way. I'm only doing
this so I have more time to explain what
to do. You would be much better off
running at 80% through your first laps.
And while doing so, you can get
acquainted with the awkward shape of
this racetrack one final time before you
roll high in turns three and four and
give yourself a straight shot to the
white flag. The corners drop off
quickly, so you'll want to use the
brakes gently to get the rear end
rotated toward the inside. Feel free to
use a bit of the apron through the
center, but don't let yourself get back
onto the throttle too hard too early.
This track is a perpetual left turn, so
if you overshoot the exit, you'll
probably be overshooting the following
corner as well. You'll also notice that
I don't go full throttle at all here.
This is by design. The rotation of the
Arca car is more reliant on the throttle
than most, so you want to leave your
lead foot at home if you want to set a
quick time here. Run both pedals like
you're dancing on eggshells, and you
could find yourself starting close to
the
front. Let's take another look.
While you have enough RPM to justify
starting in second gear, the gears are
really short here, so I would recommend
starting in third unless you have a
quick hand. Once you take the green,
your first priority should be to get as
close to the bottom as you can. At a
track as flat as this, you want to
shorten the distance around the corners
as much as possible. But keep in mind
that this car also has the turning
radius of a small bus. If you want to
get this car to rotate through the
corner, regardless of which lane you
find yourself in, you'll need the trail
break on entry. Allow the car to settle
and get the nose pointed toward the
center before leaning on the right rear
on exit. If you find yourself given the
bumper or stuck in the second lane,
you'll need to pinch the inside line to
the best of your ability. The wall comes
up fast on the straightaways, so you
really can't afford to leave any space
to be desired. Underdrive the corners if
you have to, as it's much better to be
slow in the second lane than fast into
the wall. From there, you can find a gap
on the inside, regroup, and begin your
run back up to the front. Finally,
beware of other drivers. There's always
one chaotic week on the ARA schedule,
and I believe this might be it. If you
have a faster driver behind you, and
you've established your place on the
bottom line, keep one eye in your
mirror. The apron is still open, and at
this level, overzealous drivers will
always feel inclined to take that risk.
So, be mindful of who you have around
you and be ready to react in the case of
a late lunch. If you can maintain your
position on the inside, keep the car
rolling through the corners, and avoid
the inevitable track blocking accident,
you could find yourself parked in
victory lane when it's all said and
done. Good luck.
